subject: programming-in-c
name: Programming in C
exam: TU assessment: 60% final examination set by the university, 40% internal (assignments, lab work, attendance).

units.title: Problem Solving with a Computer, and the Shape of a C Program
topics: Program, programming language and its levels
Problem solving: from a statement to a program

sections.title: Program, programming language and its levels
Problem solving: from a statement to a program

summary: Think in algorithms first; trace on paper; then code.
Pseudocode is exact English, flowcharts are exact pictures; neither depends on a language.
C is compiled, portable, close to hardware and the basis of Unix, Linux and most system software.
A C program is directives, then main, then other functions; statements end in ;.
gcc -Wall and read every warning. A program that compiles can still be wrong: test and debug.

units.title: Elements of C: Tokens, Data Types, Operators and Console Input/Output
topics: Eight common mistakes with data types, operators and input/output

sections.title: Eight common mistakes with data types, operators and input/output

summary: Tokens are keywords, identifiers, constants, strings, operators, punctuators.
Pick the type by the range you need; integer arithmetic truncates, so cast before dividing when you want a real result.
Precedence rules decide grouping; parentheses remove doubt. Never modify one variable twice in an expression.
printf formats, scanf parses; check scanf's return value and prefer fgets for lines.

units.title: Control Statements: Decisions, Loops and Jumps
topics: Eight uses of loops and decisions in real programs

sections.title: Eight uses of loops and decisions in real programs

summary: Decide with if/else if/switch; repeat with for/while/do-while.
Trace loops in a table; count iterations by hand before running.
break exits, continue skips, goto is a last resort.
The commonest bugs are = for ==, an accidental ; after for/if, missing break, and floating-point loop counters.

units.title: Arrays and Strings
topics: Eight uses of arrays and strings

sections.title: Eight uses of arrays and strings

summary: Arrays: same type, contiguous, zero-based, unchecked.
Master four loops over arrays: scan, search, swap-based sort, nested matrix loops.
Strings are char arrays ended by '\0'; the library functions all depend on it.
Overflowing an array or a string buffer is the most common serious C bug.

units.title: Functions, Recursion and Storage Classes
summary: Write small functions with one purpose and a prototype.
Remember copies are passed; use pointers for output parameters.
Recursion needs a base case; know the cost.
Know where each variable lives and how long it lasts.

units.title: Pointers and Dynamic Memory Allocation
topics: Addresses, pointers and the two operators

sections.title: Addresses, pointers and the two operators

summary: A pointer is an address with a type; * follows it, & makes it.
Array indexing is pointer arithmetic in disguise.
Strings are char sequences handled by pointer; arrays of pointers store ragged lists.
The heap gives size flexibility at the price of discipline: allocate, check, use, free.

units.title: Structures, Unions and File Handling
topics: Eight uses of structures, unions and files

sections.title: Eight uses of structures, unions and files

summary: A structure groups different types into one record; arrays of structures are tables.
A union overlays members in one block; an enum names integers.
Preprocessor lines run before compilation; parenthesise macros.
Files make data permanent: open, check, read or write, close; binary files plus fseek give random access.

units.title: The Preprocessor, the Build Process, Bit Operations and Linked Structures
topics: The build process: from source to running program
The odd loop, exit, and parameterising main
Self-referential structures, typedef and table lookup
Eight uses of the topics in this unit

sections.title: The build process: from source to running program
The odd loop, exit, and parameterising main
Self-referential structures, typedef and table lookup
Eight uses of the topics in this unit

summary: The preprocessor performs textual substitution before compilation; macros are fast but unchecked.
A C program is built in five stages; errors belong to a stage.
Bitwise operators manipulate individual bits; bit-fields pack small values.
The odd loop, exit and argc/argv complete flow control and program interfaces.
Self-referential structures give linked data; function pointers give callbacks.
